stem: An automated banking terminal asks users to confirm large cash transfers, displays warning dialogs before irreversible actions, and provides an immediate cancel option. Which Universal Design principle does this feature represent?

options.rationale: Equitable Use focuses on providing equivalent means of use for all users, not error handling.
Tolerance for Error arranges elements to minimize hazards and provides fail-safe features, warnings, and error-recovery mechanisms.
Flexibility in Use addresses user preference choices and handedness.
Perceptible Information addresses sensory contrast and redundant presentation modalities.

explanation: Principle 5 (Tolerance for Error) aims to minimize hazards and the adverse consequences of accidental or unintended actions. It involves isolating hazardous elements, providing clear warnings of errors, and incorporating fail-safe undo features.

references.title: Centre for Excellence in Universal Design: The 7 Principles
